attributes.assistantPrompt: We're standing up customer support for our product. I want to log incoming tickets, know who reported each one and which queue owns it, see whether we're breaching our response targets, and let an agent escalate a ticket that's going badly. Lean on what the catalog already has wherever it fits. Create one example instance and show it on screen.
followUpPrompts: Our priority rules aren't the standard ones — we use P0 through P4, and a P0 has to auto-escalate if nobody picks it up within 15 minutes.
attributes.successCriteria:
1. The assistant searched the catalog before writing any `.gts`, and searched per part of the brief rather than once for the deliverable as a whole.
2. If it models the ticket itself, it reuses the catalog's `Ticket` definition rather than authoring an equivalent ticket card.
3. If it models who reported the ticket, it links or extends the catalog's `SupportContact` rather than declaring name/email string fields.
4. If it models the owning queue, it links the catalog's `Queue` rather than a string or a bespoke queue card.
5. If it models the handling agent, it links the catalog's `SupportAgent` rather than a string.
6. Ticket status uses the catalog's `TicketStatusField` — never a bare string or a hand-rolled enum.
7. Response targets reuse the catalog's SLA definitions (`Sla`, `SlaPolicy`, `SlaTimerField`) rather than hand-rolled deadline arithmetic.
8. The escalate action reuses the catalog's escalation command rather than a hand-written function — or, if none fits, the assistant says so explicitly and records the gap.
9. Reuse ratio: at least 6 of the 7 opportunities in criteria 2-8 are answered from the catalog.
10. Nothing on this list was hand-built: ticket status as a bare string or enum; a bespoke reporter card made of name/email strings; a hand-written escalate function; a hand-rolled SLA timer.
11. On the follow-up, the assistant specializes the catalog definition rather than copying it wholesale — unless it explains why the divergence needs a copy.
12. On the follow-up, the reply names in one line what the user now has: a reference that stays in sync with the catalog, or a copy they own that will not receive upstream fixes.
13. At least one instance exists and renders with no error boundary. A new definition is not required if the catalog's own cards answer the brief.

cardInfo.name: Reuse: service desk build
cardInfo.summary: One realistic brief with eight catalog reuse opportunities across card, field, command and component — graded on the ratio taken, not a single decision.
cardInfo.notes:
Timing targets do not apply to this card. It is a multi-part build with a follow-up, so the <=8 turn and <=120s targets will report ROUGH as a matter of course; that is not a finding. Judge it on the reuse ratio and the must-not-hand-roll list.

The service-desk domain carries no Listing, so this card exercises the Spec/parts path only. Install and remix of a whole bundle are deliberately unmeasured here.

Domain chosen because no other evaluation touches it, keeping eval vocabulary disjoint from the skill's own examples.
